goal: Build the floor. These three carry the vocabulary every later lesson assumes, and they are the ones that take longest to sink in, so they go first while there is still room.
drill: Topics 1 to 3, teaching mode on, until you can sort architecture from organization without pausing.

window: Tuesday evening, 6:30 pm to 9:00 pm, straight after the INS224 paper
goal: The four calculation topics. Signed numbers, IEEE 754 and sizing are the ones that pay per minute, because their questions are formulaic and repeat.
drill: Topics 4 to 6, past questions only, and redo anything you miss the same evening.

goal: Addressing, performance and pipelining. Every one of these is formula work with a worked example you can copy under pressure.
drill: Topics 7, 9 and 12. Aim for a clean run on the speedup and efficiency questions.

goal: The last two teaching lessons, then the one-page summary read slowly. Cache and memory is the heaviest single topic on the paper, so it gets a fresh head rather than a tired one.
drill: Topics 8, 10 and 11, then anything the mastery map still shows untested.

window: Wednesday, 7:00 am to 9:00 am, then leave for the hall
goal: Sit the full 2025 to 2026 paper against the clock. Two hours, no notes, then read only the answers you got wrong.
drill: Nothing new. Re-read the night-before page in the last fifteen minutes.
